newsitem.title: USA: TV industry agrees new ratings system - senator.
newsitem.headline: TV industry agrees new ratings system - senator.

text.p: All of the major U.S. television networks, except NBC, have agreed on a new ratings system to add letters for sex, violence and foul language to the current age-based system, Sen. John McCain said Wednesday.

McCain, an Arizona Republican, announced the agreement reached by the television industry and leading parent groups and said it would be formally signed Thursday. The new voluntary ratings system will take effect from Oct. 1, he said.
"I think this is a great victory for the parents, this is a family victory," McCain said. "This agreement is a done deal, it will be formally signed tomorrow morning, and I am very happy about it."
The Federal Communications Commission will hold a hearing on the agreement, McCain said. He said he hoped that "would be persuasive to NBC to join."

An aide to McCain said the industry group representing cable television stations would be signing the deal, but some specific cable stations had not agreed to the ratings. Under the agreement, content ratings would be added to television programs such as S for sex, L for language, V for violence and D for dialogue.

Rep. Billy Tauzin, a Louisiana Republican, said he hoped NBC would eventually agree to implement the ratings system. "If Americans really want less violence on television, with this agreement, they'll have the tool now to stop it," he said.
